result.title: ELMA: Benchmarking Anaphoric Compositions for Long-Term Text-to-Motion Generation
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track
result.summary: Text-guided long-term human motion generation is essential for applications such as continuously operating digital avatars. Despite recent progress on short clips, existing models struggle with multi-segment instructions that involve anaphora, where constraints established in earlier segments must be preserved over time. In this paper, we introduce a novel task of long-term motion generation from such anaphoric compositions. To mitigate this, we present ELMA, an episodic long-term motion dataset with dense segment-level annotations that preserve cross-segment dependencies. Built via a fully automated collection and filtering pipeline, ELMA extracts high-quality, continuous 30-second clips from in-the-wild videos, capturing the episodic narratives necessary for long-range state modeling. Leveraging this dataset, we fine-tune state-of-the-art motion generation models to incorporate long-range context. Extensive experiments reveal fundamental shortcomings in current models when handling context-dependent instructions. We demonstrate that ELMA enables significant improvements in both global physical realism and semantic alignment, setting a robust new baseline for long-term motion synthesis.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出从含指代的长指令生成长期人体动作的新任务，并构建 ELMA：一个经自动化流水线采集、带密集分段标注、可保留跨段依赖的 30 秒情节级动作数据集，用于微调现有动作生成模型以利用长程上下文，实验显示当前模型在上下文依赖指令上存在根本缺陷。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「指代消解 + 跨段约束长期保持」与情节式长程状态建模，可能为检验 latent 状态是否保留早期任务必要条件、评估长时程信息坍缩提供类比任务与评价思路，但属动作生成领域，与 VLM 推理无直接机制联系，线索可供核查。
